title: Power & Utilities
summary: Power companies use PI System for thermal plant performance, renewables monitoring and transmission and distribution grids. Templated AF models carry heat rate, condition monitoring and event frames for downtime, startups and failures, rolled up from equipment to unit, plant and fleet.
hierarchy:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  FL[Fleet] --> PL[Plant]
  PL --> U[Unit]
  U --> PS[Primary System such as boiler, turbine, condenser]
  PS --> SS[Subsystem]
  SS --> EQ[Equipment such as a feedwater pump]
  PF[Wind Portfolio] --> WF[Wind Farm]
  WF --> T[Turbine]
  UT[Utility] --> RG[Region]
  RG --> SB[Substation]
  SB --> TX[Transformer, Breaker, Feeder or Circuit]
```

tags.name: Net MW
tags.description: Net generation: output delivered to the line after the plant's own (auxiliary) use.

tags.name: Fuel Flow
tags.description: Fuel mass flow, an input to the heat rate calculation.

tags.name: Active Power
tags.description: Actual power output of a wind turbine, compared with theoretical power.

tags.name: Dissolved Oxygen
tags.description: Boiler water chemistry measurement; an OSIsoft deck cites a limit below 10 ppb.

tags.name: Cation Conductivity
tags.description: Boiler water chemistry measurement; an OSIsoft deck cites a limit below 0.2 µS/cm.

templates.name: Wind Turbine
templates.description: Templated turbine element under a wind farm. ENTEGA compares theoretical with actual power per turbine; the attribute names are illustrative.

templates.name: Thermal Unit
templates.description: Generating unit element with performance calculations, notifications and performance curves carried on the template.

calculations.name: Heat rate
calculations.description: Fuel energy input per net kWh generated (EIA definition). Lower is better. The AF expression form is illustrative.

calculations.name: Thermal efficiency
calculations.description: EIA states 3,412 Btu equals 1 kWh, so 10,500 Btu/kWh is about 33% and 7,500 Btu/kWh about 45%.

eventFrames.name: Downtime
eventFrames.trigger: Unit stops generating; one of the power event types named by OSIsoft

kpis.name: Heat rate
kpis.definition: Energy used per net kWh generated, in Btu/kWh.

kpis.name: Production vs schedule
kpis.definition: Actual generation compared with scheduled generation.

kpis.name: Availability
kpis.definition: Share of time a unit is available to generate; Longannet reported a 12.4% improvement.

kpis.name: Theoretical vs actual power
kpis.definition: Per-turbine comparison of expected and delivered power (ENTEGA).

regulation.name: NERC CIP
regulation.summary: North American Electric Reliability Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection standards. OSIsoft decks cite them, including the Electronic Security Perimeter that limits direct access to cyber assets, when designing PI security architecture.

pitfalls: Naming conventions matter, especially for element-relative PI Vision displays (Luminant).
Document the analysis backfill sequence and know asset interdependencies before backfilling (Luminant).
Mirroring a work-management structure such as Maximo in AF can become too hard to maintain; Longannet cut its structure back to metrics only.
verifyNote: The wind turbine attribute names and the T&D level ordering are inferred; the AF form of the heat rate expression is illustrative. No readable AVEVA source on wind-turbine availability formulas (IEC 61400-26) was found.
